candidates.title: Tell No One
candidates.reason: Alexandre Beck's apparently murdered wife appears in new surveillance footage just as buried bodies and incriminating objects reopen the case. Across the film, cryptic emails, disputed forensic evidence, a safe-deposit-box trail, police pursuit, threats from hired criminals and the possibility of institutional protection progressively widen the mystery. A final confrontation exposes the staged death, the conspiracy and conflicting accounts of an earlier killing. The complete-film synopsis and Ebert's account support meaningful intermediate clues and reversals, not simply an investigation with no payoff; however, Screen Daily observes that a long climactic explanation supplies much of the ultimate causal picture and that tension flags in the last third. The New Yorker also describes the truth arriving in small increments. This is a sustained wrong-man chase, clue puzzle and corruption mystery with some violent action and emotional memories, but its crowded cast, contrived connections and backloaded explanation limit the revelation-cadence assessment.

candidates.title: No Exit
candidates.reason: Darby discovers a kidnapped child in a van outside a snowbound rest stop and initially questions four stranded strangers to identify the culprit. The complete-film account shows the first suspect identified relatively early, followed by a second accomplice reveal, a disclosure about the trafficking destination and a later betrayal by a seemingly helpful insider. Those discoveries do reframe whom Darby can trust at several stages, but most of the later runtime is a violent escape-and-countermove struggle rather than sustained evidence investigation. Ebert explicitly notes the early disclosure of the apparent central answer alongside several later chapter-like twists; the Los Angeles Times describes further surprises but doubts the film's thematic payoff, while The Guardian finds the early reveal drains the guessing game and the subsequent survival conflict repetitive. Thus suspense, deception, danger and action are stronger than deep clue-puzzling or continuously progressive revelation. The compact setting, escalating brutality and contemporary production are assets, offset by contrivances, thin characterisation and uneven tonal control.

research_rejections.title: The Hidden Face
research_rejections.reason: Its central missing-person puzzle turns on a concealed room and a major mid-film perspective change, after which the narrative chiefly follows captivity, jealousy and a final role reversal. The complete IMDb plot and Variety review represented on Rotten Tomatoes do not establish that meaningful answers repeatedly accumulate across the entire runtime; the critic calls the thrills consecutive rather than cumulative. The film has suspense and strong isolated twists, but the evidence for sustained progressive revelation is weaker than for the staged candidates.
